"""
URL: https://leetcode.com/problems/html-entity-parser/description/?envType=problem-list-v2&envId=vn57k9wr

1410. HTML Entity Parser

HTML entity parser is the parser that takes HTML code as input and replace all the entities of the special characters by the characters itself.

The special characters and their entities for HTML are:
- Quotation Mark: the entity is " and symbol character is ".
- Single Quote Mark: the entity is ' and symbol character is '.
- Ampersand: the entity is & and symbol character is &.
- Greater Than Sign: the entity is > and symbol character is >.
- Less Than Sign: the entity is < and symbol character is <.
- Slash: the entity is ⁄ and symbol character is /.

Given the input text string to the HTML parser, implement the entity parser.

Return the text after replacing the entities by the special characters.

Example 1:

Input: text = "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."
Output: "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."
Explanation: The parser will replace the & entity by &. Unknown entities like &ambassador; are left as-is.

Example 2:

Input: text = "and I quote: "...""
Output: "and I quote: \"...\""

Constraints:

    1 <= text.length <= 10^5
    The string may contain any possible characters out of all the 256 ASCII characters.
"""


class Solution:
    def entityParser(self, text: str) -> str:
        mapping = {
            """: '"',
            "'": "'",
            "&": "&",
            ">": ">",
            "<": "<",
            "⁄": "/",
        }
        # sort keys by length descending to prefer longest matches first
        keys = sorted(mapping.keys(), key=len, reverse=True)

        res = []
        i = 0
        n = len(text)
        while i < n:
            if text[i] == "&":
                matched = False
                for k in keys:
                    if text.startswith(k, i):
                        res.append(mapping[k])
                        i += len(k)
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    # No known entity matched; keep the '&' as-is
                    res.append("&")
                    i += 1
            else:
                res.append(text[i])
                i += 1
        return "".join(res)


sol = Solution()

example1 = "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."
print(sol.entityParser(example1))  # "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."

assert (
    sol.entityParser("& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not.")
    == "& is an HTML entity but &ambassador; is not."
)
assert sol.entityParser("and I quote: "..."") == 'and I quote: "..."'

assert sol.entityParser("&") == "&"
assert sol.entityParser("&&&") == "&&&"
assert sol.entityParser("&unknown; & &amp") == "&unknown; & &amp"
assert sol.entityParser("&amp;") == "&"
assert sol.entityParser("<>&"'⁄") == "<>&\"'/"
assert sol.entityParser("text &frasl text ⁄ end") == "text &frasl text / end"
assert sol.entityParser("Ends with &amp") == "Ends with &amp"
assert sol.entityParser("&⁄⁄&") == "&//&"
